title: Sapporo Grand Sumo Wants an Answer
flavor: The sumo association's organizing committee sends a lobbyist to your office. The Sapporo Grand Sumo tournament, the lobbyist says, can return every year if legislators back it. Sumo is rooted deep in Japanese culture, and a yearly tournament keeps Yezo aligned with Japan, brings visitors into local shops while it is in town, and gives students an easy way into a sport.

title: The Temple Bell Needs a Ringer
flavor: The Buddhist Temples Association is ringing the great bell at {place:shrine_temple} and asks you to take a turn. A neighbor mentions, quietly, that the bell tower roof leaks.

title: Local Newspaper Advertisement
flavor: The regional paper offers a half page. The sales representative is very persuasive.

title: National Television Spot
flavor: A producer has thirty seconds of prime time and a price list.

title: Community Grant
flavor: The local associations all have a project. You can fund one.

title: Weekend Rally
flavor: The hall is booked and a few hundred chairs are set out. The question is how you want to be remembered.

title: A Journalist Calls
flavor: A reporter you have never met asks for a few minutes about the week in the Assembly.

title: A Question About the Street
flavor: A shopkeeper stops you outside {place:station}. The road surface has been broken for years, and everyone keeps talking about a faster train but nobody says who pays.

title: Neighborhood Festival Invitation
flavor: The association is holding {place:festival} on the weekend and has saved you a place at the head table.

title: A Rumor in the Hall
flavor: Something you said, or something people think you said, is traveling the corridors.

title: A Constituent Writes
flavor: A handwritten letter from a resident arrives with a stamp that was clearly licked twice.

title: The Treasurer Drops By
flavor: The party treasurer stops at your door and mentions, pleasantly, that the dues are coming.

title: A Veteran Writes About the Coast
flavor: A veterans' hall secretary writes that the old coastal batteries at {place:landmark} are being discussed again, and nobody has asked the people who served there.

title: The Mayors Ask for Ten Minutes
flavor: Three mayors catch you in a corridor. They want to talk about who pays for what between the prefecture and the towns.

title: A Priest Asks About the Old Gate
flavor: A temple priest and a shrine caretaker from {office_city} have come together, which almost never happens, to ask about the gate that both their congregations use.

title: A Founder Pitches You on the Train
flavor: A young founder recognizes you on {place:travel_route}, sits down uninvited, and has a laptop open before you can say no.

title: A Reception Invitation
flavor: An embassy sends a card for a reception: black tie, short speeches, and a guest list heavy with retired officers.

title: A Hotel Owner Cannot Find Staff
flavor: The owner of a small hotel in Noboribetsu waits until the end of your office hours. Two floors are shut because she cannot hire anyone, and the visitors keep coming.

title: A Shop Clerk Shows You Her Pay Slip
flavor: She puts the slip on the counter and does not say anything. The number speaks for itself.

title: A Parents' Meeting
flavor: {place:school} invites you to a parent-teacher night. The talk turns to what children are, and are not, being taught.

title: A Long-Time Resident Asks Why He Cannot Vote
flavor: He has paid local taxes for thirty years, coaches the youth team, and was born two streets from here. He cannot vote.

title: The Clinic Is Closing on Fridays
flavor: A nurse from the village clinic at {place:onsen_town} says the doctor now comes only four days a week, and the next clinic is ninety minutes away.

title: A Harbor Customs Officer Writes
flavor: A letter in careful handwriting from {place:harbor}: the harbor is short of staff, the paperwork has doubled, and no one in the capital seems to know.

title: Buy a Local Radio Spot
flavor: The regional station has a slot between the weather and the traffic report. It is cheap and everyone listens.

title: Sponsor a Local Sports Team
flavor: The youth baseball club needs new shirts and a van. The coach is polite about asking.

title: Appear on a Podcast
flavor: A popular podcast about regional politics has asked you for an hour. The host is friendly and well prepared.

title: Constituency Office Open Day
flavor: You open the doors for a morning, put out tea and wait to see who comes.

title: Sponsor a Festival Float
flavor: The {place:festival} committee needs a sponsor for the lead float. Your name would go on a banner.

title: A Radio Host Calls
flavor: A morning radio host asks if you can be on air in ten minutes, live, no script.

title: A School Asks You to Visit
flavor: A teacher at {place:school} writes that the class has been studying the Assembly and would like a real legislator to answer questions.

title: A Dispute Over a Trash Site
flavor: Two neighborhoods in Kitami both refuse the new transfer station. Each wants you to say it should go to the other.

title: A Photograph Goes Around
flavor: A picture of you at a stall in {place:market} is being shared. It is not a bad picture. People you do not know are writing to you.

title: A Local Official Retires
flavor: A town official you have worked with for years retires. The farewell is small, and held in a meeting room.

title: Heavy Snow Closes the Road
flavor: Overnight snow has shut the road up to Sukayu in the Hakkōda Mountains. The village office calls to ask whether anyone in the capital is listening.

title: A Bear Is Seen Near a School
flavor: The principal of {place:school} calls at seven in the morning. A bear has been seen at the edge of the school grounds.

title: A Union Delegation Waits Outside
flavor: Six people in matching jackets stand politely outside your office. They have petitions in plastic folders.

title: A Reminder From Party Headquarters
flavor: An envelope with the party crest, addressed in a clerk's careful hand. Inside is a statement of what your account still owes, and a line asking when it might be settled.

title: The Treasurer Brings the Receipts
flavor: The treasurer is passing through the district and has asked for ten minutes. A folder of receipts is tucked under one arm.

title: An Invitation to the Party Fundraiser
flavor: A printed card for the regional fundraising dinner. Tickets are not cheap, but the head table seats people who matter.

title: The Prime Minister's Opening Address
flavor: The National Assembly is full for the opening of the session. The Prime Minister rises to set out the government's agenda, and every party is watching how the others take it.

title: Morning Radio Exercises at {place:landmark}
flavor: A group of elders has done the same radio exercises on the path at {place:landmark} every morning for decades. The organizer asks whether you would join them for the first set.

title: Ainu Cultural Showcase Day
flavor: {place:ainu_site} is holding its cultural showcase day: songs, dance, embroidery and food. The elders have asked whether you will come.

title: A College Visit to an Ainu Cultural Center
flavor: A university student society has invited you to join its field visit to {place:ainu_site}. The students will tour the exhibits and meet the staff, and they would like a legislator to come along.

title: The Station Wants a Debate
flavor: The regional station is putting two guests head to head on tomorrow's morning show: you, and a representative of a local organization who has plenty to say about you.

title: Students Ask for a Campus Q&A
flavor: Students United has booked the biggest lecture hall at {place:university} and asked you to take their questions. They say they will not go easy on you.

title: The Fisheries Cooperative Calls a Meeting
flavor: The Fisheries Cooperative has called its members to the hall at {place:harbor} about quotas, prices and the cracked breakwater, and asked you to stand in front of them.

title: The Chamber Wants a Breakfast Speech
flavor: The Chamber of Commerce has a breakfast of fifty business owners booked and an empty slot for a legislator.

title: A Newspaper Wants a Profile
flavor: A national paper is running profiles of legislators to watch and wants an hour with you, at your office, with a photographer.

title: The Co-op Invites You to the Harvest
flavor: The agricultural cooperative at {place:farmland} is bringing in the autumn harvest and invites you to spend a few hours in the fields with its members.

title: A Workshop Opens on the Shopping Street
flavor: A woodcarver and two potters have opened a shared workshop in an empty shop at {place:market}. The Artisans Guild asks you to cut the ribbon.

title: Commuters Ask You to Ride the Rush-Hour Train
flavor: The Commuter Committee dares you to ride the packed rush-hour train on {place:travel_route} with them, standing, before you next speak on fares.

title: The Taxpayers' Alliance Sends a Scorecard
flavor: The Taxpayers' Alliance is grading every legislator on spending and wants your answers to twenty questions about it.

title: A Bank Asks for a Roundtable
flavor: The Financial Industry Association wants you to chair a roundtable on lending to small firms in the district.

title: A Consumer Group Brings a Complaint File
flavor: The Consumer Advocacy Network arrives with a box of complaints about hidden fees and asks you to take it to the ministry.

title: The Two Neighborhoods Meet
flavor: You convened both Kitami neighborhood associations in one room, as you said you would. Nobody wants the transfer station, and everyone has come.

title: The Ministry Replies About the Harbor
flavor: The ministry has answered the letter you forwarded from {place:harbor}: the harbor office will be reviewed, at some point, by someone.

title: The Airline Writes Back
flavor: The airline has answered your question about a direct route to Mongolia, with thanks and a passenger survey.

title: A Delegation Comes for Cultural Exchange
flavor: A cultural delegation from abroad is touring the capital this week. Their host asks whether you will welcome them, and what Yezo will put on the table.

title: Honoring the Elders at the Hall
flavor: The neighborhood association in {office_city} is honoring every resident over eighty and asks you to hand out the certificates.

title: Litter After the Blossom Parties
flavor: After a week of cherry-blossom parties, Hirosaki Park is buried in cans and paper.

title: A Car That Never Moves
flavor: A rusted car has sat outside the apartment blocks in Ebetsu for half a year. The residents want it gone.

title: The Farm Road Washes Out
flavor: Last night's storm took out the only road to six farms near {place:farmland}. The co-op asks whether you will come and see it.

title: Old Campaign Boards Still Standing
flavor: Poster boards from an old campaign are still up on three corners, your own face among them, peeling.

title: A Supporter's Grandson Is Getting Married
flavor: An elder of Local Kōenkai invites you to her grandson's wedding reception in Hachinohe, where the bride's family lives.

title: The Ditch That Floods
flavor: Every heavy rain, the drainage ditch behind the housing complex in Iwamizawa overflows into the yards, and the mosquitoes follow.

title: Will You Lend Your Name?
flavor: The organizers of a charity run around Lake Ōnuma for the children's hospital ask whether they can list you as an honorary patron.

title: The Streetlight Is Back On
flavor: Hanako Okuda writes: the corner light came on last night. She asks whether the next corner could be next.

title: The Passport Arrives in Time
flavor: Chihiro Endo's passport arrived two days before the flight. A reporter from the Hokkaido evening paper has heard about it and wants the story.

title: The Crows Move One Street Over
flavor: The nets work on Hanako Okuda's street in Kotoni. The crows have moved to the next one, and its association is at your door.

title: The Pothole Is Patched
flavor: The pothole on the road into Hakodate's morning market is filled. The delivery drivers have left a thank-you note and a box of doughnuts at your office.

title: The Veteran's Claim Comes Back
flavor: The ministry has approved the Nemuro coast guard veteran's claim. The Veterans' Association invites you to a small celebration at its hall.

title: The Owner of the Empty House Is Found
flavor: The town has traced the owner of the empty house in Imabetsu to Sapporo. He wants to sell, but not to pay for the demolition.

title: The Phone Company Writes Back
flavor: A carrier will survey the Yūbari valley road for a tower, if the town provides the land at no charge.

title: The Scam Calls Come Again
flavor: Ayako Kudo calls from Obihiro: since your session, two of her clients hung up on scammers. A third was not there, and lost her savings.

title: The Wind Turbine Meeting
flavor: The village hall near {place:energy_site} is full. The company has brought a model of the turbine, and the sheep farmers have brought their questions.

title: The Auditor's Report Is Out
flavor: An audit of a district program has come back with a long list of unexplained costs, and the Taxpayers' Alliance wants to know what you will do about it.

title: The Budget Hearing Draws a Crowd
flavor: A budget hearing at the district hall draws more citizens than seats. The Taxpayers' Alliance asks you to back a freeze on one local fee.

title: The Chamber Hosts a Trade Fair
flavor: The Chamber of Commerce is opening a regional trade fair and asks you to cut the ribbon and stay for the afternoon.

title: A Foreign Buyer Visits {place:harbor}
flavor: A buyer from overseas wants a large order of local goods and asks whether the permits can move quickly. The Chamber of Commerce wants an answer.

title: The Shopping Street Wants Late Hours
flavor: Shopkeepers at {place:market} want evening hours extended. Residents nearby are worried about the noise. The Small Business Owners' Association asks for your support.

title: The Family Shop Faces a New Rule
flavor: A small family shop cannot afford a new compliance form. The Small Business Owners' Association asks you to press for a simpler one.

title: The Bank Offers a Small Loan Scheme
flavor: The Financial Industry Association proposes a loan scheme for new businesses and asks you to endorse its terms.

title: A Savings Fair at {place:community_hall}
flavor: The Financial Industry Association is running a free workshop on scams and savings at {place:community_hall}. The Family Network is holding a picnic at the same time.

title: The Startup Demo Day
flavor: Young founders pitch to a hall full of neighbors, and the Innovation Society asks you to name the proposal you liked best.

title: The Data Center Wants the Old Mill
flavor: A firm wants to turn a closed mill into a data center. The Innovation Society and the Chamber of Commerce back it. Some nearby residents fear losing the old building.

title: The Old Craft Fair Needs Support
flavor: A century-old craft fair asks for your name on its patron list and for its stall fees to be waived this year.

title: The Hall's Roof Is Failing
flavor: {place:community_hall}, which hosts the district's festivals, needs a new roof. Our Traditional Society asks you to back a public grant.

title: A Committee Clerk Needs a Signature
flavor: A committee clerk catches you in the corridor with a schedule change that moves a colleague's hearing to Thursday. It needs a member's signature by the end of the day.

title: A Member From Another Party Asks You to Co-Sign
flavor: A member from across the aisle asks you to co-sign a small amendment to the order of debate. It changes little, they say, but a second party's name would help.

title: The Press Gallery Wants a Word After the Vote
flavor: The vote ends early and the press gallery empties into the corridor. Two reporters wait by the stairs with the same question: what did you make of it?

title: A Lobbyist Leaves a Gift Basket
flavor: A gift basket arrives at your office from a business group, with a card that hopes you are keeping well. The fruit is excellent. The card is very friendly.

title: The Session Runs Late
flavor: The debate runs past the dinner hour and the chamber thins out. Whoever stays will be noted, and whoever leaves will be noted too.

title: The Party Faction Invites You to Lunch
flavor: Members of your party's faction have a table booked for lunch and an empty chair. Nothing is on the agenda, which usually means something is.

title: A Budget Annex Arrives Without a Summary
flavor: The Ministry of Finance has sent the annex to a spending bill, three hundred pages and no summary, with a note that members are welcome to ask questions.

title: A School Group Visits the Gallery
flavor: A class from a school in your district is in the visitors' gallery on a day trip. Their teacher has asked whether you might say hello before they go home.

title: A Rival's Aide Offers to Compare Notes
flavor: An aide to a member of a rival party stops you after the hearing and offers to compare notes on who is saying what in the corridors. They would like the same from you.

title: The Labor Federation Asks for a Seat at the Table
flavor: Three delegates from the Labor Federation wait outside the committee room with a folder and the polite persistence of people who have waited before.

title: A Student Asks About the Fare
flavor: A student across the aisle recognizes you. Her season ticket just went up again, she says, and half her class commutes the same line.

title: A Fisherman Heading Home
flavor: A man in rubber boots sits down heavily beside you, smelling faintly of the harbor. The catch was poor this week, he says, and the ice plant wants more for the same ice.

title: A Reporter Recognizes You on the Platform
flavor: A reporter from the national media is on the same carriage, notebook already in hand. "One question, if you have a minute. Everyone on this train has a minute."

title: A Farmer With a Crate of Vegetables
flavor: A farmer is carrying a crate of radishes to a cousin in the city, and he has opinions about the price support scheme that he has never had the chance to share with a member.
image: TRAIN_INTERIOR; TRAIN_INTERIOR_2; TRAIN_INTERIOR_3; TRAIN_INTERIOR_4; TRAIN_INTERIOR_5; TRAIN_INTERIOR_6

title: A Commuter Complains About the Delays
flavor: The train has been held at a signal for ten minutes. The commuter standing next to you says this happens every week and nobody ever answers for it.

title: A Colleague From Your Party Is Aboard
flavor: A member of your own party is two seats down, and has noticed you. They lean over with the particular smile of someone who is about to ask for something.
